"""Run python server.py --port 6380 in a terminal. Listens only on 127.0.0.1."""
import argparse
import asyncio
import time

from session import Session

def connection_handler(records):
    async def handle(reader, writer):
        session = Session(records)
        try:
            while not session.closed:
                chunk = await reader.read(65536)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                now_ms = time.monotonic_ns() // 1_000_000
                writer.write(session.feed(chunk, now_ms))
                await writer.drain()
        except (ConnectionResetError, BrokenPipeError):
            pass
        finally:
            writer.close()
            try:
                await writer.wait_closed()
            except (ConnectionResetError, BrokenPipeError):
                pass
    return handle

async def main(port):
    server = await asyncio.start_server(connection_handler({}), "127.0.0.1", port)
    async with server:
        print(f"Listening on 127.0.0.1:{server.sockets[0].getsockname()[1]}", flush=True)
        await server.serve_forever()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=6380)
    try:
        asyncio.run(main(parser.parse_args().port))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass

"""With the server running, use python demo.py --port 6380 in a second terminal."""
import argparse
import socket

def request(*args):
    frame = [b"*" + str(len(args)).encode() + b"\r\n"]
    for arg in args:
        frame += [b"$" + str(len(arg)).encode() + b"\r\n", arg, b"\r\n"]
    return b"".join(frame)

def expect(stream, expected):
    result = stream.read(len(expected))
    if result != expected:
        raise AssertionError(f"Expected {expected!r}, received {result!r}")
    print(repr(result))

def main(port):
    addr = ("127.0.0.1", port)
    with socket.create_connection(addr, timeout=3) as first, socket.create_connection(addr, timeout=3) as second:
        with first.makefile("rb") as first_input, second.makefile("rb") as second_input:
            value = b"A\x00\r\n\xff"
            packet = request(b"SET", b"lab:demo", value)
            first.sendall(packet[:9])
            second.sendall(request(b"PING"))
            expect(second_input, b"+PONG\r\n")
            first.sendall(packet[9:])
            expect(first_input, b"+OK\r\n")
            second.sendall(request(b"GET", b"lab:demo") + request(b"DEL", b"lab:demo"))
            expect(second_input, b"$5\r\n" + value + b"\r\n:1\r\n")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=6380)
    main(parser.parse_args().port)

class Examples(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_example_1(self):
        request = {'events': [{'at': 10,
             'client': 'writer',
             'wire': '*5\r\n'
                     '$3\r\n'
                     'SET\r\n'
                     '$1\r\n'
                     'k\r\n'
                     '$1\r\n'
                     'v\r\n'
                     '$2\r\n'
                     'PX\r\n'
                     '$1\r\n'
                     '5\r\n'},
            {'at': 14,
             'client': 'reader',
             'wire': '*2\r\n$3\r\nGET\r\n$1\r\nk\r\n'},

             'client': 'reader',

            {'at': 1, 'client': 'B', 'wire': '*1\r\n$4\r\nPING\r\n'},

             'client': 'A',

        expected = {'pending': {'A': 3},
 'replies': ['', '+PONG\r\n', '+PONG\r\n$2\r\n\x00ÿ\r\n']}

# Build a Redis-compatible TCP server

Two clients share a keyspace. One sends half a request and pauses. The other pipelines a SET and a GET containing a newline and a zero byte. Implement the server that decodes the stream, applies commands, and sends each reply to the right socket. Then connect two real clients to the same code on localhost.

## Implementation scope

Build the RESP2 request parser, in-memory byte store and command dispatcher. The project supplies the asyncio listener, connection buffering and a replay adapter. The server handles PING [message], SET key value [PX ms], GET key and DEL key [key ...]. Data lives for the lifetime of a single server process. The tests focus on stream fragmentation, command ordering, binary values and expiration.

## Input

Pass {"events": [...]} to gateway.handle. Each ordered event contains at (integer milliseconds), client (connection ID), and either wire (a string of bytes that arrived) or close: true. In JSON one Latin-1 code point represents one byte, so \r\n is the RESP delimiter and \u00ff is byte FF. A client ID opens a connection on its first read and can reconnect after a close. Times never decrease.

## Output

Return {"replies": [...], "pending": {...}}. replies[i] contains all wire bytes generated by event i, in command order. An incomplete frame or disconnect emits an empty string. pending maps each still-connected client with buffered data to its unread byte count. A new replay starts with empty storage and connections.

## Constraints

Every request is a nonempty RESP2 array of up to 1024 bulk strings, each at most 65536 bytes. Use the supplied header() grammar. A command takes effect at the timestamp of the chunk that completes its frame. Preserve byte-valued keys and values, including empty strings. A malformed frame emits the protocol error, discards the remaining stream and closes that connection. A valid but unsupported or misused command emits the documented command error and processing continues.

## Example 1

Input

~~~json
{
  "events": [
    {
      "at": 10,
      "client": "writer",
      "wire": "*5\r\n$3\r\nSET\r\n$1\r\nk\r\n$1\r\nv\r\n$2\r\nPX\r\n$1\r\n5\r\n"
    },
    {
      "at": 14,
      "client": "reader",
      "wire": "*2\r\n$3\r\nGET\r\n$1\r\nk\r\n"
    },
    {
      "at": 15,
      "client": "reader",
      "wire": "*2\r\n$3\r\nGET\r\n$1\r\nk\r\n"
    }
  ]
}
~~~

Output

~~~json
{
  "replies": [
    "+OK\r\n",
    "$1\r\nv\r\n",
    "$-1\r\n"
  ],
  "pending": {}
}
~~~

The writer sets k at 10 ms with PX 5. A second connection sees v at 14 ms. At exactly 15 ms GET returns a RESP null bulk string.

## Example 2

Input

~~~json
{
  "events": [
    {
      "at": 0,
      "client": "A",
      "wire": "*1\r\n$4\r\nPI"
    },
    {
      "at": 1,
      "client": "B",
      "wire": "*1\r\n$4\r\nPING\r\n"
    },
    {
      "at": 2,
      "client": "A",
      "wire": "NG\r\n*2\r\n$4\r\nPING\r\n$2\r\n\u0000\u00ff\r\n*2\r"
    }
  ]
}
~~~

Output

~~~json
{
  "replies": [
    "",
    "+PONG\r\n",
    "+PONG\r\n$2\r\n\u0000\u00ff\r\n"
  ],
  "pending": {
    "A": 3
  }
}
~~~

A's first PING is incomplete. B has a separate receive buffer and replies immediately. The last read finishes A's PING, echoes two binary bytes, and retains the three bytes of a third request.

## Part 1 · Frame a TCP byte stream

Use header() to consume an array length and one bulk-length header per argument. Read exactly the promised payload bytes and its two-byte CRLF. Return only the first complete command and its consumed length. On incomplete input return None, leaving buffering to Session. A malformed type, empty array, out-of-range length or invalid complete terminator raises ProtocolError.

protocol.py · parse_request(data) — Return (list of bytes arguments, consumed byte count) for the first complete frame, None for an incomplete frame, or raise ProtocolError for a malformed frame. Use header() with limits 1024 arguments and 65536 bytes per bulk string. Reject empty command arrays.

## Part 2 · Own the clock and the keyspace

Implement the shared map of byte keys to (value, absolute_deadline_or_None). Enforce expiry on read and delete. A plain overwrite clears the old deadline. DEL counts each live key removed, including keys containing empty byte values.

store.py · lookup(records, key, now_ms) — Return the live bytes value, or None for missing/expired keys. A deadline is exclusive: expire and remove the record when now_ms >= expiry_ms.

store.py · put(records, key, value, now_ms, ttl_ms=None) — Replace any old record, setting an absolute deadline of now_ms + ttl_ms. A missing TTL clears any prior expiry. The dispatcher validates TTLs.

store.py · delete_many(records, keys, now_ms) — Delete keys and return the count of live entries removed. Missing, expired and repeated keys contribute zero after their first removal.

## Part 3 · Dispatch commands and serve real clients

Use ARITY for invalid PING/GET/DEL arity or SET missing key/value. SET with extra arguments accepts exactly PX and its duration; use SYNTAX for other extension shapes and EXPIRY for invalid duration (requires 1–9 ASCII digits and positive value). Use UNKNOWN for unsupported commands. Bare PING replies +PONG; PING with a message and GET return bulk strings. Successful SET replies +OK and DEL returns a RESP integer. Every response ends in CRLF. Start server.py and run demo.py from a second terminal.

commands.py · bulk(value) — Encode None as a null bulk string and bytes as a length-prefixed string.

commands.py · execute(records, args, now_ms) — Return RESP2 bytes for PING [message], SET key value [PX ms], GET key or DEL key [key ...]. Ignore ASCII case in the verb and PX. Validate before writing. See constants for the four command errors.

## Run locally

Standard-library Python 3.10 or newer. Start at gateway.py to trace the request.

~~~sh
python run_lab.py fixtures/example_1.json
python -m unittest discover -s tests
~~~

## Run the service locally

From the extracted starter, run python server.py --port 6380. In a second terminal run python demo.py --port 6380. The demo opens two connections, fragments a SET and checks the exact binary reply from a pipelined GET and DEL. You can also send individual commands with redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6380 PING. Stop the server with Ctrl+C.

## Reading

- [Redis · RESP wire protocol](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/reference/protocol-spec/)

- [Redis · SET and expiration](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/set/)

- [Redis · PING](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/ping/)

- [Redis · DEL](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/del/)
